feedback.problem:
Given that the expression $\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)$ can be written as $R\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x-ϕ)$ with ${0}^{∘}<ϕ<{90}^{∘}$ and $R>0,$ what is the value of $ϕ?$

$ϕ=$ 
{{field-1}}${}^{∘}$
feedback.worked_solution:
The difference formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x-ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ-\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)-R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x-ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)-(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x),$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=\sqrt{2} \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =1 \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =1 \\ ϕ & =45\,{\,}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$
